To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

supercritical CO2 treatment under addition of small amounts of water, hydrogenperoxide and acetic acid is a gentle, effective and non-cytotoxic alternative to conventional sterilization procedures like ethylene oxide treatment, steam and gamma sterilization.

we developed a scCO2 based sterilization procedure which effectively inactivates a wide spectrum of microorganisms and is less compromising on mechanical properties and cell viability than other established sterilization methods.
supercritical carbon dioxide treatment is an effective and gentle sterilization method for biomaterials that are sensitive to established sterilization methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bioresorbable materials for medical application and the optimization of sterilization procedures for these materials.
the development of novel bioresorbable implant materials for the repair of bone defects and the development of novel, non-cytotoxid, non-cytostatic sterilization methods for these materials.
the development of novel bio-resorbable materials and their sterilization by means of supercritical CO2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

scCO2 treatment with the addition of water, peroxide and acetyl groups (e.g. acetic anhydroide) is a very effective and gentle, non-cyotoxic sterilization method especially applicable to biomaterials.

scCO2 treatment is a gentle and effective sterilization method with regard to the inactivation of microorganisms, the mechanical stability as well as the cytocompatibility of biomaterials and thus a promising method for sterilization of bioresorbable implant materials.
scCO2 treatment is an effective and gentle sterilization method for a broad range of sensitive biomaterial applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scCO2 sterilisation procedure developed in this work is effective, gentle, fast and non-cytotoxic.
we developed and tested a novel sterilization process for the terminal sterilisation of sensitive implant materials like bioresorbable scaffolds and hydrogels for regenerative medicine applications.
we have shown the feasibility to sterilize a wide range of sensitive biomaterial with supercritical carbon dioxide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supercritical CO2 sterilization is a promising alternative for the terminal sterilisation of sensitive biomaterial.
scCO2 can be used for sterilizing biomaterials without compromising their properties or their cytocompatibility.
scCO2 can be a very effective and gentle alternative sterilization technique for biomaterials and medical devices.
